builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents TVM Manchester Ltd (TVM Sound), incorporated in 1957 and manufacturing amplifiers and PA equipment in the 1960s-70s, alongside a surviving TVM Fuzz Box whose physical features are distinctly 1960s.
relationship_status: Exact fuzz production date and total run remain unknown; no OEM attribution is needed for qualification.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible as a rare historical dirt maker; keep production date provisional.

dirt_product_evidence: Vox by EF-EL Distortion; EUR Distortion family
builder_evidence: Effects Database identifies the rare Italian-made late-1960s Vox by EF-EL Distortion as produced by EF-EL (Calderoni Musica), and identifies related EF-EL branded/OEM products. The product is explicitly classified as a fuzz despite the marketed Distortion name.
relationship_status: Customer-brand relationships across Vox, Goldsound, G.I.S., EUR, Silversound and others remain separate lineage questions.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible as a physical Italian dirt manufacturer; do not create duplicate builders for its customer labels.

builder_evidence: Roger Mayer's own history says he designed his first fuzz guitar effects pedal in 1964; Vintage Guitar records that he designed and made fuzzboxes for Jimmy Page and Big Jim Sullivan, while Fuzzboxes documents his general-public fuzz advertising by 1966.
relationship_status: Original 1964 work was custom rather than conventional production. Later commercial history must remain a separate period.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible under a custom/micro-builder class; do not present early Mayer units as mass-production pedals.

builder_evidence: Historical research documents Rhodes creating a fuzz circuit in California and making multiple small metal-box fuzz units for professional musicians, including Nokie Edwards of the Ventures and Billy Strange; the Rhodes fuzz was used on the Ventures' 1962 recording of The 2,000 Pound Bee.
relationship_status: No commercial production line is established; this is a custom-builder lineage.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible under a custom/micro-builder class; distinguish from Gibson/Maestro commercial manufacture and do not assume the later Maestro Fuzz-Tone was simply a Rhodes-branded product.

dirt_product_evidence: Custom fuzz box for Jeff Beck
builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents an early Jeff Beck fuzz box built for him by Tridents bandmate Paul Lucas. This establishes a custom dirt device but not yet a broader independent builder operation.
relationship_status: One-off provenance is strong but wider builder identity and production scope are unresolved.
recommended_treatment: Keep research-only/provisional until additional independent evidence of custom production is found.

builder_evidence: Retail advertising establishes that Clifford sold or advertised fuzz boxes, but surviving evidence does not establish that Clifford manufactured them.
recommended_treatment: Exclude from builder census; retain only as retail/distribution history if relevant to a future pedal record.
